concepts.name: Chilika Lake: Ecology, Location and Ramsar Designation
key_dimensions: Largest coastal lagoon in India and largest wintering ground for migratory birds in the Indian subcontinent
Located in Odisha at the mouth of Daya River draining into Bay of Bengal — distinction from other coastal lakes
First Indian wetland to be designated under Ramsar Convention (1981); also first to be removed from Montreux Record and then restored
Irrawaddy dolphin habitat — UPSC trap on which lake hosts this endangered species vs. Gangetic dolphin

concepts.name: Wular Lake: Largest Freshwater Lake in India
key_dimensions: Located in Jammu & Kashmir (Bandipora district) — formed by tectonic activity, fed by Jhelum River
Distinction trap: Wular is largest natural freshwater lake in India vs. Vembanad (largest lake by area overall) vs. Pangong (highest)
Ramsar-designated wetland; listed under Montreux Record due to degradation from siltation and weed infestation
Strategic importance — part of Indus Waters Treaty considerations; role in flood moderation for Kashmir Valley

concepts.name: Vembanad Lake: Largest Lake in India by Area and Backwater Ecology
key_dimensions: Longest lake in India and largest by surface area — spans Kerala districts including Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam
Ramsar site; part of Kerala Backwaters system — distinction between backwater (kayal) and lagoon geography
Thanneermukkam Bund divides it into freshwater (north) and saline (south) sections — UPSC trap on salinity gradient
Nehru Trophy Boat Race held here — Kuttanad region ('Rice Bowl of Kerala') lies below sea level within this watershed

concepts.name: Pangong Tso: High-Altitude Transboundary Lake
key_dimensions: Highest large lake in India (~4,350m); located in Ladakh — extends into Tibet/China (60% in China, 40% in India)
Endorheic (no outlet) saline lake despite being fed by glacial streams — trap: students assume high-altitude lakes are freshwater
Ramsar site — strategic significance highlighted during 2020 Galwan standoff; Finger Area geography
Not part of Indus basin drainage — drains into Shyok tributary region; freezes completely in winter

concepts.name: Dal Lake: Urban Wetland and Ecological Threats
key_dimensions: Located in Srinagar, J&K — fed by springs and streams draining Zabarwan range; no natural outlet (semi-endorheic)
Ramsar site under threat — Montreux Record listing due to encroachment, sewage, and weed (Trapa/water chestnut) invasion
Distinction from Wular: Dal is urban lake within city vs. Wular is natural tectonic lake in open valley
Floating gardens (Rad) and houseboats — unique human-lake interface tested in environment questions

concepts.name: Loktak Lake: Largest Freshwater Lake in Northeast India and Phumdis
key_dimensions: Located in Manipur — largest freshwater lake in Northeast India (not entire India — common UPSC trap)
Famous for phumdis — floating biomass islands unique to this lake; Keibul Lamjao National Park is the world's only floating national park
Ramsar site; listed on Montreux Record — threatened by Ithai Barrage (hydroelectric) causing water level rise destroying phumdis
Habitat of endangered Sangai (Manipur brow-antlered deer) — only found here; extinction risk linkage

concepts.name: Sambhar Lake: Largest Saline Lake in India
key_dimensions: Located in Rajasthan (Nagaur and Jaipur districts) — largest inland saline lake in India; in arid Thar Desert region
Tectonic origin (inter-montane basin) fed by seasonal rivers Mendha, Rupangarh, Khari — endorheic basin
Ramsar site — wintering ground for flamingos; salt production since ancient times under Sambhar Salts Ltd.
UPSC trap: Sambhar = largest saline inland lake; Chilika = largest coastal lagoon; Wular = largest freshwater — all three distinctions in one question

concepts.name: Lonar Lake: Meteoric Crater Lake — Unique Origin
key_dimensions: Located in Buldhana district, Maharashtra — only known hyper-velocity impact crater in basaltic rock in the world
Both saline AND alkaline (high pH ~10–11) — unique dual chemistry; hosts extremophile microorganisms including haloalkaliphiles
Ramsar site (designated 2020) — surrounded by dense forest; geological and astrobiological research significance
Crater age debated (~50,000–570,000 years) — UPSC may test on its origin type vs. volcanic crater lakes like Anshi

concepts.name: Tsomoriri (Moriri) Lake: High-Altitude Ramsar Wetland in Ladakh
key_dimensions: Located in Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, Ladakh at ~4,522m — higher than Pangong Tso in elevation
Ramsar site — habitat of bar-headed goose, black-necked crane (endangered); only breeding ground of black-necked crane in India
Endorheic saline lake — no outlet; fed by snowmelt and springs; freezes in winter
Distinction trap: Tsomoriri vs. Pangong — both in Ladakh, both saline, both Ramsar, but Tsomoriri is higher and hosts black-necked crane

concepts.name: Kolleru Lake: Freshwater Lake Between Two River Deltas
key_dimensions: Located between Krishna and Godavari deltas in Andhra Pradesh — one of the largest freshwater lakes in India
Ramsar site; also a Wildlife Sanctuary — fed by seasonal streams Budameru and Tammileru; drains into Krishna via Upputeru
Severe encroachment for aquaculture (prawn farming) — Montreux Record listing; Supreme Court ordered eviction of illegal fish farms
Distinction: Kolleru is natural freshwater lake between two deltas — unlike Pulicat (saline lagoon on AP-TN border)

concepts.name: Pulicat Lake: Second Largest Coastal Lagoon and Flamingo Habitat
key_dimensions: Located on Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border (mostly in AP) — second largest coastal lagoon after Chilika
Separated from Bay of Bengal by Sriharikota Island (ISRO launch site) — barrier island geography trap
Major flamingo habitat in South India; Pulicat Lake Bird Sanctuary; fed by Arani and Kalangi rivers
Not a Ramsar site — UPSC trap: students assume all major bird lakes are Ramsar designated; Pulicat is NOT on Ramsar list

concepts.name: Tso Kar: White Lake and Salt Pan in Ladakh
key_dimensions: Located in Changthang plateau, Ladakh — named 'White Lake' due to salt encrustation on shores; shallow saline lake
Ramsar site (2020, same batch as Lonar) — part of Tso Kar Wetland Complex including Startsapuk Tso (freshwater)
Breeding ground of bar-headed goose and black-necked crane — distinction from Tsomoriri which is more famous for same species
Salt extraction by nomadic Changpa community — human-ecosystem interface; traditional livelihoods angle

concepts.name: Bhoj Wetland (Upper and Lower Lakes of Bhopal): Man-Made Ramsar Site
key_dimensions: Located in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh — Upper Lake (Bada Talab) built in 11th century by Raja Bhoj; one of the oldest man-made lakes
Ramsar site covering both Upper (natural + modified) and Lower Lake — drinking water source for Bhopal city
Threatened by urban encroachment, sewage, and weed infestation — Montreux Record implications
UPSC trap: man-made lakes CAN be Ramsar sites — students often assume only natural wetlands qualify

concepts.name: Sasthamkotta Lake: Largest Freshwater Lake in Kerala
key_dimensions: Located in Kollam district, Kerala — largest natural freshwater lake in Kerala (distinction from Vembanad which is a backwater/lagoon)
Ramsar site — unique self-purifying quality attributed to presence of Chaoborus (phantom midge) larvae that filter bacteria
Drinking water source for Kollam district — protected under Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act
UPSC trap: Vembanad vs. Sasthamkotta — Vembanad is largest overall lake in Kerala but Sasthamkotta is largest purely freshwater natural lake

concepts.name: Renuka Lake: Largest Natural Lake in Himachal Pradesh
key_dimensions: Located in Sirmaur district, Himachal Pradesh — largest natural lake in the state; shaped like a reclining woman
Ramsar site — religious significance (associated with Goddess Renuka); adjacent to Renuka Wildlife Sanctuary with lion safari
Fed by Renuka River (tributary of Giri, which joins Yamuna) — drainage pattern linkage
Distinction: Renuka = largest in HP; Chandratal and Surajtal are higher altitude lakes in HP but smaller and in Lahaul-Spiti

concepts.name: Chandratal and Surajtal: High-Altitude Himalayan Lakes in Himachal Pradesh
key_dimensions: Chandratal (~4,300m) in Lahaul-Spiti — crescent-shaped glacial lake; source of Chandra River (joins Bhaga to form Chenab)
Surajtal (~4,890m) near Baralacha La — one of the highest lakes in India; source of Bhaga River
Chandratal is Ramsar site; Surajtal is NOT — common trap about which Himalayan lakes have Ramsar status
Both are oligotrophic glacial lakes — seasonal accessibility; ecological sensitivity to climate change and glacial retreat

concepts.name: Hussain Sagar Lake: Man-Made Lake and Pollution Issues
key_dimensions: Located in Hyderabad, Telangana — built in 1562 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah on Musi River tributary; heart-shaped lake
Famous for Buddha statue on Gibson Rock island in the middle of the lake — collapsed during installation (1990)
Severely polluted by industrial effluents and sewage from twin cities — not a Ramsar site; contrast with Bhoj Wetland
UPSC trap on man-made lakes of historical significance in peninsular India — often confused with Nagarjuna Sagar (dam reservoir on Krishna)

concepts.name: Naini Lake (Nainital): Glacial Lake in Uttarakhand Kumaon Hills
key_dimensions: Located in Nainital, Uttarakhand — kidney/crescent-shaped glacial lake at ~2,084m; origin debated between glacial and landslide-dammed
Drainage: no natural inlet river visible — fed by underground springs and rainwater; drains via Ballia Nala into Kosi River system
UPSC trap: Nainital lake is NOT a Ramsar site despite being a well-known lake — awareness of Ramsar gaps
Landslide of 1880 caused major disaster — geological instability of the region; carrying capacity concerns for tourism

concepts.name: Ashtamudi Lake: Eight-Armed Lake and Mangrove Ecosystem
key_dimensions: Located in Kollam district, Kerala — second largest wetland in Kerala after Vembanad; named for its eight (ashta) arms (mudi)
Ramsar site — gateway to Kerala backwaters from the south; connected to Vembanad-Kol wetland system
Rich mangrove ecosystem; important for clam and fish harvesting — sustainable fisheries and livelihood angle
Distinction: Ashtamudi = southern gateway backwater in Kollam; Vembanad = central Kerala backwater — both Ramsar, both in Kerala

concepts.name: Indian Ramsar Wetlands — Pattern, Criteria and Recent Additions
key_dimensions: India has 80+ Ramsar sites (as of 2024) — largest number in South Asia; Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of Ramsar sites among states
Ramsar criteria (9 criteria) — UPSC tests on which criterion applies: waterbird threshold (Criteria 6: >20,000 waterbirds), threatened species habitat, representative wetland type
Recent additions: Karikili, Pallikaranai marsh, Pichavaram (Tamil Nadu); Sakhya Sagar, Sirpur (MP); Ranwari, Bakhira — pattern of state-wise distribution
Montreux Record trap: being on Montreux Record does NOT remove Ramsar status — it flags ecological change; India currently has sites both listed and delisted from Montreux Record
